problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 D300 DT306 Suffers Premature Wear
problems.rootCause: Early-production tensioner design prone to premature wear, leading to chain rattle, misfires, and potential catastrophic engine damage if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Installing an updated OEM-spec timing chain kit with revised tensioner.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended at 60k miles on pre-2022 models as a preventative measure.

repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the chain has already jumped or secondary damage has occurred.

problems.recommendation: For pre-2022 DT306 units with under 60,000 miles, a preventative timing chain upgrade is strongly advised. However, if chain noise, oil dilution, or misfires are already present, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded internals offers the best long-term reliability and preserves your high-value Defender investment.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Leaks & Oil Dilution - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 D300 DT306 Loses Oil Integrity
problems.rootCause: Frequent short-trip driving triggers aggressive DPF regenerations, washing unburnt fuel into the crankcase and overwhelming the PCV system, alongside EGR cooler internal leaks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full oil and filter change with engine flush, plus PCV valve and EGR inspection.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early with no bearing knock or severe sludge.
